title: Series & parallel circuits
examples: What is the difference between series and parallel circuits?
How do I calculate the total resistance in a circuit?
If I add more bulbs in series, what happens to the brightness?

explain.say: Today we will learn about two types of circuits. These are series and parallel circuits.
In a series circuit, the current must flow through every component. The current is the same everywhere.
In a parallel circuit, the current splits to go through different paths. The total current is the sum of the paths.
For voltage, the total voltage is always divided among the components. This is called voltage drop.
The total resistance is different for both types. In series, resistances add up directly.
In a parallel circuit, the total resistance is less than the smallest single resistance. This is a key rule.

faq.q: Does the total voltage always add up in a series circuit?
faq.a: Yes, the total voltage supplied by the source equals the sum of the voltage drops across each component.
asks: How do I calculate voltage in series?
Is Vtotal always V1 plus V2?

faq.q: If I add more bulbs in parallel, what happens to the current?
faq.a: Adding more paths in parallel increases the total current drawn from the source.
asks: How does adding a branch affect Itotal?

faq.q: Is the total resistance always higher in series or parallel?
faq.a: The total resistance is always higher in a series circuit than in a parallel circuit with the same components.
asks: Does series or parallel give higher Rtotal?

faq.q: If I remove a bulb in a series circuit, what happens?
faq.a: The circuit breaks, and no current can flow through any of the remaining components.
asks: What happens if one bulb blows in series?
Does one break stop the whole series circuit?

faq.q: Does the current have to be the same in all parts of a parallel circuit?
faq.a: No, the current splits. Each branch will draw a different amount of current depending on its resistance.
asks: Is I in parallel always equal?
Can current be different in parallel paths?

facts: In a series circuit, the current is the same everywhere.
In a parallel circuit, the total current is the sum of the individual branch currents.
Total voltage in a series circuit is the sum of individual voltage drops.
Total resistance in series circuits adds up: Rtotal = R1 + R2 + ...
Total resistance in parallel circuits is always less than the smallest individual resistance.

quiz.say: Three resistors of 2 ohms are connected in series. What is the total resistance?
quiz.why: In series, the total resistance is found by adding all the individual resistances together.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you must add the resistances together, not use the smallest value.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you cannot simply divide the resistance by the number of components.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you are not finding the average resistance; you must sum them up.

quiz.say: Two resistors of 4 ohms are connected in parallel. What is the total resistance?
quiz.why: For parallel, you add the reciprocals of the resistances first, then find the reciprocal of the sum.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the total resistance must be less than the smallest single resistance.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you cannot simply multiply the resistances together.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you are not finding the average; you must use the reciprocal formula.

quiz.say: If a 12 volt battery powers two lamps in series, and each lamp has a 4 ohm resistance, what is the voltage across one lamp?
quiz.why: The total voltage is divided equally between the two identical components in series, so 12 divided by 2 is 6.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the voltage drop is related to the resistance, not just the resistance value.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you cannot add the voltage twice; the total voltage is given by the battery.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the voltage splits across the components; it does not stay the same.
